Implement score, lives and active-play timing

Unit 1 · Week 9 · Lesson 3 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the current Year 11 project brief, project-workbook.md, project-milestones.csv, project-test-log.csv and the selected scenario starter in project-pack.zip. Check the four S01 preparation exits first. Use the shared FR/NFR contract at https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/assessments/games/year11-requirements.md . Keep school-issued support, assessment and submission conditions visible. Use a disposable local folder, synthetic labels, primitive shapes and permitted static assets. Suggested times are untrialled; record actual completion/support and re-plan openly if needed.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

Current project workbook · Shared game requirements · Project test log · Ten workshop milestones

1. Integrate lives and active-play timing

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Milestone and learning intention

Contract FR4/FR5: zero lives or zero remaining time causes loss; loss is resolved before win if conditions coincide in one update. No score changes after a result. The displayed hit times assume a consistent elapsed hit clock and first accepted hit at1000 ms; state your implementation’s time base and pause policy. The shared pause contract freezes gameplay time/movement. Do not use blocking sleeps for protection. The expected table is a plan until observed in the student build. 5. Check a plan before changing code

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided plan/trace clinic

Use a short dry-run, role explanation or peer critique only where school conditions permit it. Each student retains their own design, code and observations. Ask for the first expected state and evidence source rather than supplying a complete assessed solution. 6. Independent workshop

Suggested time: 25 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent milestone with optional scaffold

Reserve this 25-minute block for the learner’s own milestone. Support by returning to one preparation example or asking a diagnostic question; record help received. Do not add optional features or imply homework completes the workshop budget. Follow school conditions for collaboration, tools, AI and permitted code.
